segments.en: Hello, English learners.
segments.zh: 各位英语学习者，大家好。

segments.en: Welcome back to another advanced lesson with us here at EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 欢迎回到 Englishpod 与我们一起参加另一个高级课程。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: And my name is Erica.
segments.zh: 我的名字是埃里卡。

segments.en: So, today we're bringing you another advanced lesson and this time it's kind of historical.
segments.zh: 所以，今天我们为您带来另一个高级课程，这一次是历史性的。

segments.en: Like the name suggests, we are listening in as a president says goodbye to the nation before he steps down from his role as president.
segments.zh: 顾名思义，我们正在听取总统在辞去总统职务之前告别国家的声音。

segments.en: Now actually this dialogue is very much based on President Eisenhower's farewell speech.
segments.zh: 实际上，这种对话很大程度上是基于艾森豪威尔总统的告别演说。

segments.en: Ah, okay.
segments.zh: 啊，好的。

segments.en: So a pretty famous...
segments.zh: 所以很有名...

segments.en: Now we have to tell you that we did change the speech a little bit, right?
segments.zh: 现在我们必须告诉你，我们确实稍微改变了演讲，对吧？

segments.en: Just a little bit to make it a little bit more understandable.
segments.zh: 只是一点点让它更容易理解。

segments.en: But it's basically what he said to the nation back in 1969.
segments.zh: 但这基本上是他在 1969 年对国家所说的话。

segments.en: Alright now, I will as well tell you that this is a pretty hard dialogue.
segments.zh: 好吧，我会告诉你，这是一个非常艰难的对话。

segments.en: It is very hard because the structures are a little bit complicated and even to a certain point a little bit poetic, right?
segments.zh: 这很难，因为结构有点复杂，甚至在某种程度上有点诗意，对吧？

segments.en: So why are we taking this speech as our dialogue?
segments.zh: 那么，为什么我们将这次演讲视为我们的对话呢？

segments.en: What are we going to learn from this?
segments.zh: 我们将从中学到什么？

segments.en: Well, we're going to learn some structures and some words that you can use maybe on a resignation letter or maybe in a celebration you want to thank Pete for coming.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们将学习一些结构和一些单词，您可以在辞职信中使用，或者在您想感谢皮特的庆祝活动中使用这些单词。

segments.en: Okay, so we're going to learn some pretty difficult vocabulary but also learn some really useful structures like you said you could use in a resignation letter or even in a formal speech of your own.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们将学习一些非常困难的词汇，但也要学习一些非常有用的结构，就像你说的你可以在辞职信中使用，甚至在你自己的正式演讲中使用。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Now, this presidential farewell speech is divided into two parts.
segments.zh: 现在，这次总统告别演说分为两部分。

segments.en: So today we're going to do part one and then next time we'll finish the speech with part two.
segments.zh: 所以今天我们将做第一部分，然后下次我们将完成第二部分的演讲。

segments.en: So let's listen to President Eisenhower as he says goodbye to the nation and we'll come back just in a little bit.
segments.zh: 因此，让我们听听艾森豪威尔总统与国家告别，我们稍后会回来。

segments.en: Good evening, my fellow Americans.
segments.zh: 晚上好，我的美国同胞。

segments.en: Three days from now, after a half-century of service to our country, I shall lay down the responsibilities of office as in a traditional and solemn ceremony, the authority of the presidency is vested in my successor.
segments.zh: 三天后，在为国家服务半个世纪之后，我将卸下公职的职责；在传统而庄严的仪式上，总统的权力将移交给我的继任者。

segments.en: This evening I come to you with a message of leave taking and farewell and to share a few final thoughts with you, my countrymen.
segments.zh: 今晚，我向各位同胞告别，并与大家分享临别前最后的一些想法。

segments.en: Like every other citizen, I wish the new president and all who will labor with him, Godspeed.
segments.zh: 同其他每一位公民一样，我祝愿新总统及与他共事的所有人一切顺利。

segments.en: I pray that the coming years will be blessed with peace and prosperity for all.
segments.zh: 我祈愿未来的岁月能给所有人带来和平与繁荣。

segments.en: Our people expect their president and the Congress to find essential agreement on questions of great importance, the wise resolution of which will better shape the future of our great nation.
segments.zh: 人民期待总统与国会在重大问题上达成必要共识，明智地解决这些问题，为我们伟大的国家创造更美好的未来。

segments.en: My own relations with Congress began on a remote and tenuous basis when long ago a member of the Senate appointed me to West Point.
segments.zh: 我与国会最初的联系既遥远又微弱：很久以前，一位参议员推荐我进入西点军校。

segments.en: I then had the pleasure of building more intimate relationships with Congress during the war and the immediate post-war period.
segments.zh: 后来，在战争期间及战后初期，我有幸与国会建立了更加密切的关系。

segments.en: Finally, we have progressed to the mutually interdependent relationship we've had during these past eight years.
segments.zh: 最终，我们发展成了过去八年间这种相互依存的关系。

segments.en: Wow, so Eisenhower is a pretty good speaker, isn't he?
segments.zh: 哇，所以艾森豪威尔是一个很好的演讲者，不是吗？

segments.en: A good speaker and well, he said a lot of really nice things when he was saying goodbye.
segments.zh: 一个很好的演讲者，嗯，他在说再见时说了很多非常好的话。

segments.en: Yeah, pretty inspiring, I thought.
segments.zh: 是的，很鼓舞人心，我想。

segments.en: Really inspiring and as we said, there were a couple of different and difficult words and phrases, so why don't we start right now with Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 真的很鼓舞人心，正如我们所说，有几个不同且困难的单词和短语，所以我们为什么不现在就从语言要点开始。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Well, Eisenhower said that in three days he shall lay down the responsibilities.
segments.zh: 好吧，艾森豪威尔说，他将在三天后卸下职责。

segments.en: To lay down the responsibilities.
segments.zh: 卸下职责。

segments.en: All right, lay down something.
segments.zh: 好吧，lay down something（放下某物）。

segments.en: Basically, we understand the verb to lay down, right?
segments.zh: 基本上，我们理解 lay down 这个动词，对吧？

segments.en: To put it down, to put it on the ground.
segments.zh: 放下，把它放在地上。

segments.en: Right, now he's using it with responsibilities which is a little bit strange but it's kind of like a metaphor by saying lay down arms, to lay down your weapons.
segments.zh: 对，现在他把它和 responsibilities（职责）搭配，有点奇怪，但有点像说 lay down arms，也就是放下武器，算是一种比喻。

segments.en: Right, and you know what?
segments.zh: 对，你知道吗？

segments.en: This is a really common phrase that we would hear especially when we're talking about the end of a war or something like that.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常常见的短语，尤其是当我们谈论战争结束或类似的事情时。

segments.en: To lay down your arms, lay down your weapons.
segments.zh: 放下武器，交出武器。

segments.en: Yeah, so here I think Eisenhower is kind of referencing this and giving us a little bit of poetry in his speech.
segments.zh: 是的，所以我认为艾森豪威尔在某种程度上引用了这一点，并在他的演讲中给了我们一点诗意。

segments.en: Right, so it's not that he's quitting, it's not that he's being fired, he's just like finishing what he started.
segments.zh: 是的，所以不是他辞职了，不是他被解雇了，他就像完成了他开始的事情。

segments.en: Yes, so he's laying down his responsibilities.
segments.zh: 是的，所以他正在放下自己的责任。

segments.en: Now, I think this would be quite an interesting phrase to use for example in a resignation letter.
segments.zh: 现在，我认为这将是一个非常有趣的短语，例如在辞职信中使用。

segments.en: Right, so I would say a month from now I will lay down my responsibilities as manager.
segments.zh: 是的，所以我会说一个月后我会放下我作为经理的职责。

segments.en: Yep, all right, so that sounds pretty good.
segments.zh: 是的，好吧，所以听起来不错。

segments.en: Now, he said he's going to be laying down the responsibilities in a traditional and solemn ceremony.
segments.zh: 现在，他说他将在一个传统而庄严的仪式上放下责任。

segments.en: All right, solemn.
segments.zh: 好吧，庄严。

segments.en: Now, solemn, what does that mean?
segments.zh: 现在，庄严，这是什么意思？

segments.en: What is a solemn ceremony?
segments.zh: 什么是庄严的仪式？

segments.en: Well, a solemn ceremony would be a serious, respectful and a little bit sad ceremony.
segments.zh: 好吧，一个庄严的仪式将是一个严肃、尊重和有点悲伤的仪式。

segments.en: Okay, so it's a serious matter and it's very respectful, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，这是一件严肃的事情，而且非常尊重，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, so you might say for example on the 11th of November when you're remembering the war you might say something like this is a very solemn day.
segments.zh: 是的，所以你可能会说，例如在 11 月 11 日，当你记得战争时，你可能会说这样的事情是非常庄严的一天。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: Okay, and the authority of the presidency is vested in my successor.
segments.zh: 好的，总统职位的权威归于我的继任者。

segments.en: Okay, so interesting verb.
segments.zh: 好吧，很有趣的动词。

segments.en: So interesting word, vested.
segments.zh: 很有意思的词，vested。

segments.en: Vested.
segments.zh: 授予；归属。

segments.en: The authority vested in my successor.
segments.zh: 权威授予我的继任者。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So this word basically means power that I have by law.
segments.zh: 所以这个词基本上是指法律赋予我的权力。

segments.en: Right, so this power, this important power you have is given to you by the law, by the president, by the country.
segments.zh: 对，所以这种权力，这种重要的权力，是法律、总统、国家赋予你的。

segments.en: This is a very common word you will hear in a wedding when the priest or the person that's leading the wedding will say by the power vested in me by the state of California.
segments.zh: 这个词在婚礼上很常见：牧师或主持婚礼的人会说 by the power vested in me by the state of California（凭借加利福尼亚州赋予我的权力）。

segments.en: Yeah, I now pronounce you husband and wife.
segments.zh: 是的，我现在宣布你们成为夫妻。

segments.en: I now pronounce you husband and wife.
segments.zh: 我现在宣布你们夫妻。

segments.en: So he's saying the power that I have given to me by the state of California I can now make you be married.
segments.zh: 所以他是说，凭借加利福尼亚州赋予我的权力，我现在可以让你们结为夫妻。

segments.en: So here Eisenhower is saying the authority of the presidency is vested in my successor.
segments.zh: 所以艾森豪威尔在这里说总统职位的权威归属于我的继任者。

segments.en: So the power of the presidency will be given to the next president by law.
segments.zh: 因此，总统的权力将由法律赋予下一任总统。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And he also wished the new president and everyone with him, he said Godspeed.
segments.zh: 他还祝愿新总统以及所有与他共事的人，他用了 Godspeed 这个词。

segments.en: All right, Godspeed.
segments.zh: 好吧，Godspeed（祝一切顺利）。

segments.en: Godspeed.
segments.zh: 祝一切顺利。

segments.en: I wish you Godspeed.
segments.zh: 祝你一路顺风。

segments.en: Now, Godspeed, what does that mean?
segments.zh: 现在，Godspeed，这是什么意思？

segments.en: Well, it's kind of a blessing.
segments.zh: 嗯，这是一种祝福。

segments.en: It basically means good luck and good fortune.
segments.zh: 这基本上意味着好运和好运。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And especially in a journey.
segments.zh: 尤其是在旅途中。

segments.en: Yeah, I think you'd almost only use this when someone's going off on a big trip or a journey.
segments.zh: 是的，我想你几乎只会在有人去大旅行或旅行时使用它。

segments.en: So here they're going on the journey of the presidency.
segments.zh: 所以这里是说，他们将踏上总统任期这段旅程。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So I wish you Godspeed.
segments.zh: 所以我祝你一路顺风。

segments.en: Godspeed.
segments.zh: 祝一切顺利。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And now let's take a look at our last set of words.
segments.zh: 现在让我们来看看我们最后一组单词。

segments.en: When he was talking about Congress, he said that his relation with Congress began on a remote and tenuous basis.
segments.zh: 当他谈到国会时，他说他与国会的关系始于一个遥远而脆弱的基础。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So two interesting words here, remote and tenuous.
segments.zh: 所以这里有两个有趣的词，遥远而脆弱。

segments.en: Now, remote, we understand as being far away or distant.
segments.zh: remote 这个词，我们知道是遥远、疏远的意思。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: What about tenuous, though?
segments.zh: 那 tenuous 呢？

segments.en: But tenuous is kind of unimportant or not really relevant.
segments.zh: tenuous 有点不太重要，或者说没什么实质关联。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So actually, this is a pretty high quality, useful and smart sounding word.
segments.zh: 实际上，这是一个相当高级、实用、听起来很聪明的词。

segments.en: So I think we should hear a few more examples of how it's used.
segments.zh: 所以我认为我们应该听到更多关于它如何使用的例子。

segments.en: Example one.
segments.zh: 例句一。

segments.en: How can you say the earth is actually getting cooler?
segments.zh: 你怎么能说地球其实在变冷呢？

segments.en: That is a pretty tenuous argument.
segments.zh: 这个论点相当站不住脚。

segments.en: Example two.
segments.zh: 例句二。

segments.en: John believes that Elvis Presley is still alive.
segments.zh: 约翰相信埃尔维斯普雷斯利还活着。

segments.en: He's got a tenuous hold on reality.
segments.zh: 他对现实的把握很脆弱。

segments.en: Example three.
segments.zh: 例句三。

segments.en: You're making yourself seem more important than you are.
segments.zh: 你让自己看起来比你更重要。

segments.en: The connection between our company's success and your performance is tenuous at best.
segments.zh: 我们公司成功与你的业绩之间的联系，最多也只能说很牵强。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So as we said, these are some pretty difficult words that we found in the dialogue.
segments.zh: 正如我们所说，这些是我们在对话中发现的一些非常困难的词。

segments.en: But now I want to go and look at some really interesting formal structures that Eisenhower used here.
segments.zh: 但现在我想去看看艾森豪威尔在这里使用的一些非常有趣的正式结构。

segments.en: So let's look at those now in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 所以让我们看看现在在流利表达中的那些。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: On Fluency Builder today, we have three phrases.
segments.zh: 今天在流利表达上，我们有三个短语。

segments.en: And well, starting with the first one, I think it's one of the most interesting ones.
segments.zh: 好吧，从第一个开始，我认为它是最有趣的之一。

segments.en: He said, three days from now, after half a century of service of our country, I shall lay down the responsibilities of office.
segments.zh: 他说，三天后，为我国服务了半个世纪后，我将放下职责。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So what's interesting about this?
segments.zh: 那么这有什么有趣的呢？

segments.en: If you take a look at the structure, he's saying three days from now, which is future, and then he makes a reference to the past after a half century of service.
segments.zh: 如果你看看这个结构，他说 three days from now，这是未来，然后他又提到过去——半个世纪的服务。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we've got future past.
segments.zh: 所以顺序是未来、过去。

segments.en: And then again, future, I shall lay down the responsibilities.
segments.zh: 然后又回到未来，I shall lay down the responsibilities（我将卸下职责）。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this actually is quite a good structure if you're giving a farewell speech or even I could imagine using this at a wedding.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您要进行告别演讲，甚至我可以想象在婚礼上使用它，这实际上是一个相当不错的结构。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: How would you use it in a wedding?
segments.zh: 你会如何在婚礼中使用它？

segments.en: I might say, 12 hours for now after a long and beautiful relationship, this couple shall marry.
segments.zh: 我可以说，12 小时后，在一段漫长而美好的关系之后，这对夫妇将步入婚姻。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So you're making reference to the future and then a past event or something that's been going on for a while and then future again.
segments.zh: 所以你先提到未来，然后是一个过去的事件、或持续了一段时间的事，然后回到未来。

segments.en: Why don't we do one more example?
segments.zh: 我们为什么不再做一件事？

segments.en: So for example, in a resignation letter, I can say, one month from now, after 30 years of hard work and dedication to this company, I shall lay down my responsibilities as product manager.
segments.zh: 举个例子，在一封辞职信里，我可以说：一个月后，在为公司辛勤奉献三十年后，我将卸下我作为产品经理的职责。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Interesting.
segments.zh: 有意思。

segments.en: So we can use it and it sounds good.
segments.zh: 所以我们可以使用它，听起来不错。

segments.en: It sounds very professional.
segments.zh: 听起来很专业。

segments.en: And very poetic.
segments.zh: 而且很有诗意。

segments.en: Very poetic.
segments.zh: 很有诗意。

segments.en: It sounds nice.
segments.zh: 听起来不错。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's a good structure.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个很好的结构。

segments.en: Now, why don't we go on to this next kind of very formal and helpful in a very formal speech?
segments.zh: 接下来我们看下一个，这在正式演讲中非常正式，也非常有用。

segments.en: Well, President Eisenhower said, this evening I come to you with a message of leave taking and farewell.
segments.zh: 好吧，艾森豪威尔总统说，今晚我来向你们传达离任与告别的讯息。

segments.en: So this evening I come to you with a message of leave taking and farewell.
segments.zh: 所以，今晚我带着离任与告别的讯息来到你们面前。

segments.en: So it's a very nice way of saying, I'm talking to you today because I am saying goodbye.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个很好的表达方式，我今天和你说话，因为我在说再见。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: And what I really like about this phrase is the beginning part.
segments.zh: 我真正喜欢这句话的是开头部分。

segments.en: This evening I come to you with a message of.
segments.zh: 今晚我带着一条消息来找你。

segments.en: So again, let's suppose we're at a wedding.
segments.zh: 再说一遍，假设我们正在参加婚礼。

segments.en: If I'm offering a toast or I'm the best man, I could say, this evening I come to you with a message of love and trust and respect.
segments.zh: 如果我要敬酒，或者我是伴郎，我可以说，今晚我带着爱、信任与敬意的讯息来到你们面前。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Or maybe if you're the leader of a company, you might say something like, this afternoon I come to you with a message of hope for the future.
segments.zh: 或者，如果你是一家公司的领导者，你可能会说，今天下午我带着对未来的希望的信息来找你。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And now the part when he says leave taking and farewell, it's basically saying taking leave or taking like a vacation, right?
segments.zh: 现在看他说 leave taking and farewell 这部分，基本上就是说告别、离开，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And farewell is goodbye.
segments.zh: 告别是再见。

segments.en: And what about our last phrase?
segments.zh: 最后一个短语是什么呢？

segments.en: This is actually a bit of a long one.
segments.zh: 这实际上有点长。

segments.en: So I'm going to read it now.
segments.zh: 所以我现在要读它。

segments.en: Our people expect their president and the Congress to find essential agreement on questions of great importance, the wise resolution of which will better shape the future of our great nation.
segments.zh: 人民期待总统与国会在重大问题上达成必要共识，明智地解决这些问题，为我们伟大的国家创造更美好的未来。

segments.en: Okay, great.
segments.zh: 好，太好了。

segments.en: So let's take a look at the first part.
segments.zh: 所以让我们来看看第一部分。

segments.en: Basically he's saying the people expect the president and the Congress to give them answers, right?
segments.zh: 基本上他是说人民希望总统和国会给他们答案，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: To agree on important issues.
segments.zh: 就重要问题达成一致。

segments.en: But in the part when he says the wise resolution of which will better shape the future of our great nation.
segments.zh: 但他说到的这部分是：the wise resolution of which will better shape the future of our great nation。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And this is the part I want to focus on.
segments.zh: 这是我想要关注的部分。

segments.en: The wise resolution of which.
segments.zh: the wise resolution of which——明智地解决这些问题。

segments.en: Now this is a really wonderful sort of formal structure.
segments.zh: 现在这是一种非常棒的正式结构。

segments.en: So we can see what he's doing here.
segments.zh: 所以我们可以看到他在这里做什么。

segments.en: He's talking about the first idea, right?
segments.zh: 他在谈论第一个想法，对吧？

segments.en: So the president and the Congress need to find agreement on important issues, right?
segments.zh: 所以总统和国会需要就重要问题达成一致，对吧？

segments.en: Now the wise resolution of which.
segments.zh: 然后是 the wise resolution of which。

segments.en: So he's referring back to that idea.
segments.zh: 所以他指的是这个想法。

segments.en: So the wise resolution of what?
segments.zh: 那么，所解决的是什么呢？

segments.en: Of the essential agreement on questions of great importance.
segments.zh: 就是前面说的在重大问题上达成必要共识。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So really useful structure.
segments.zh: 所以非常有用的结构。

segments.en: Why don't we hear a few more examples of this?
segments.zh: 为什么我们没有听到更多的例子呢？

segments.en: Example one, we now face a great challenge, the overcoming of which lead us all to untold riches and success.
segments.zh: 示例一，我们现在面临着一个巨大的挑战，克服了这些挑战，使我们所有人都获得了无与伦比的财富和成功。

segments.en: Example two, we as a company now face our most difficult months to date, the outcome of which will determine our company's future.
segments.zh: 示例二，我们作为一家公司现在面临着迄今为止最困难的月份，其结果将决定我们公司的未来。

segments.en: Example three, the ambitious plan to reduce poverty, the start of which was launched last Tuesday in New York, will require a huge investment of taxpayers' dollars.
segments.zh: 示例三，这项雄心勃勃的减贫计划上周二在纽约启动，它将需要大量纳税人资金投入。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So as you can hear from the examples, we have the main idea and then he passes on, but then kind of refers back to it again.
segments.zh: 因此，正如您从示例中听到的那样，我们有主要想法，然后他继续前进，但随后又重新引用了它。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And this sounds quite formal, but also quite literary and intelligent.
segments.zh: 这听起来很正式，但也相当有文采、有智慧。

segments.en: It makes you sound well-spoken.
segments.zh: 它让你显得很有口才。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: This was quite a difficult dialogue with some really interesting and tricky structures and words.
segments.zh: 这是一个相当困难的对话，有一些非常有趣和棘手的结构和文字。

segments.en: Let's hear it one more time all together.
segments.zh: 让我们再一起听一遍。

segments.en: Good evening, my fellow Americans.
segments.zh: 晚上好，我的美国同胞。

segments.en: Three days from now, after a half-century of service to our country, I shall lay down the responsibilities of office as in a traditional and solemn ceremony, the authority of the presidency is vested in my successor.
segments.zh: 三天后，在为国家服务半个世纪之后，我将卸下公职的职责；在传统而庄严的仪式上，总统的权力将移交给我的继任者。

segments.en: This evening, I come to you with a message of leave taking and farewell, and to share a few final thoughts with you.
segments.zh: 今晚，我带着离任与告别的讯息来到你们面前，并与你们分享几点最后的想法。

segments.en: My countrymen, like every other citizen, I wish the new president and all who will labor with him Godspeed.
segments.zh: 我的同胞，和其他所有公民一样，我希望新总统和所有与他一起工作的人 Godspeed。

segments.en: I pray that the coming years will be blessed with peace and prosperity for all.
segments.zh: 我祈愿未来的岁月能给所有人带来和平与繁荣。

segments.en: Our people expect their president and the Congress to find essential agreement on questions of great importance, the wise resolution of which will better shape the future of our great nation.
segments.zh: 人民期待总统与国会在重大问题上达成必要共识，明智地解决这些问题，为我们伟大的国家创造更美好的未来。

segments.en: My own relations with Congress began on a remote and tenuous basis when, long ago, a member of the Senate appointed me to West Point.
segments.zh: 我本人与国会的关系始于一个遥远而脆弱的基础上：很久以前，一位参议员推荐我进入西点军校。

segments.en: I then had the pleasure of building more intimate relationships with Congress during the war and the immediate post-war period.
segments.zh: 后来，在战争期间及战后初期，我有幸与国会建立了更加密切的关系。

segments.en: Finally, we have progressed to the mutually interdependent relationship we've had during these past eight years.
segments.zh: 最终，我们发展成了过去八年间这种相互依存的关系。

segments.en: All right, we're back, and here with us in the studio we have Pete, the actor in the dialogue of President Eisenhower's presidential farewell speech.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们回来了，演播室里还有 Pete，他就是艾森豪威尔总统告别演讲对话里的演员。

segments.en: He's a pretty convincing actor at that.
segments.zh: 他是一个非常有说服力的演员。

segments.en: Not quite.
segments.zh: 也算不上。

segments.en: So, Pete is going to give us a little bit of insight about President Eisenhower.
segments.zh: 所以，皮特将给我们一些关于艾森豪威尔总统的见解。

segments.en: All right, so what can you tell us about President Eisenhower?
segments.zh: 好吧，关于艾森豪威尔总统，你能告诉我们什么吗？

segments.en: Well, he started off as a general.
segments.zh: 好吧，他最初是一名将军。

segments.en: He was an accomplished officer all through the early 20th century, and then he was the supreme commander of the Allied Expeditionary Force in World War II.
segments.zh: 他是整个 20 世纪初的一名有成就的军官，然后他是二战中盟军远征军的最高指挥官。

segments.en: And so now he's most famous for D-Day.
segments.zh: 所以现在他最出名的是诺曼底登陆日。

segments.en: He was leading it?
segments.zh: 是他指挥的吗？

segments.en: Or he was on the battlefield?
segments.zh: 还是他在战场上？

segments.en: No, he was the organizer.
segments.zh: 不，他是组织者。

segments.en: He was kind of like the brains behind the operation.
segments.zh: 他算是这次行动背后的智囊。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: I don't know if you want to leave this in, but there's a really cool document that he wrote right before the invasion, and it said he basically knew this was going to go one of two ways, and he wrote down a script to read in case it failed.
segments.zh: 我不知道你想不想保留这段，但他登陆前写过一份很酷的文件；大意是他知道结果只会有两种可能，于是写下了一份备用讲稿，以防行动失败时宣读。

segments.en: And he basically said, you know, I'm sorry to inform you that the invasion did not go as planned, and this is setback our war effort.
segments.zh: 他大意是说：很遗憾地通知各位，登陆没有按计划进行，这使我们的战事受到挫折。

segments.en: And when the invasion went well, he threw that in the trash, and then one of his aides found that and was like, wow, this is a historical document.
segments.zh: 结果登陆顺利，他就把那份讲稿扔进了垃圾桶；后来他的一名副官发现了它，惊叹道，哇，这是一份历史文献。

segments.en: And they kept the...
segments.zh: 他们保留了...

segments.en: Oh, really?
segments.zh: 哦，真的吗？

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So they had the copy.
segments.zh: 所以他们有副本。

segments.en: Alternate history.
segments.zh: 架空历史。

segments.en: All right, so he was an accomplished general, an amazing warrior.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以他是一个有成就的将军，一个了不起的战士。

segments.en: But what about his presidency?
segments.zh: 但是他的总统职位呢？

segments.en: Well, at the beginning, probably the biggest thing he did was to wrap up the Korean War, which was a vow he made during his campaign.
segments.zh: 嗯，一开始，他最大的政绩大概就是结束朝鲜战争，这是他在竞选期间许下的承诺。

segments.en: And then he visited Korea.
segments.zh: 然后他访问了韩国。

segments.en: Obviously the war is still technically on, but they did arrange a ceasefire.
segments.zh: 严格来说，战争至今仍未正式结束，但他们促成了停火。

segments.en: Eisenhower built up the interstate highway system, which is one of the big reasons that America was able to become economically successful in the 20th century.
segments.zh: 艾森豪威尔建立了州际公路系统，这是美国能够在 20 世纪取得经济成功的重要原因之一。

segments.en: He did it basically so that in case of a war, we'd have an easy way of shipping our soldiers and nukes across the country.
segments.zh: 他这样做基本上是为了在战争的情况下，我们可以轻松地将我们的士兵和核武器运送到全国各地。

segments.en: But it worked well anyways.
segments.zh: 但无论如何它都运作良好。

segments.en: Yeah, it's one of these things that pays a side benefit.
segments.zh: 是的，这是其中之一，可以带来额外的好处。

segments.en: At least he had to sell it to the country that way.
segments.zh: 至少他得用那种说法把它推销给全国民众。

segments.en: It's very likely that he didn't intend ever to use it that way.
segments.zh: 他很可能不打算以这种方式使用它。

segments.en: But you have to have...
segments.zh: 但你必须有...

segments.en: It's like the war on terror.
segments.zh: 这就像反恐战争。

segments.en: You got to sell these things.
segments.zh: 你得会把这些东西推销出去。

segments.en: Well, and I guess it's had a huge impact not only on the economy of the states, but also like the culture and the way that people view the car and its effect on society.
segments.zh: 好吧，我想它不仅对各州的经济产生了巨大的影响，而且对人们的文化和看待汽车的方式及其对社会的影响也产生了巨大的影响。

segments.en: Definitely.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: So pretty influential guy, this Eisenhower.
segments.zh: 如此有影响力的家伙，这个艾森豪威尔。

segments.en: Yeah, and a very historical lesson.
segments.zh: 是的，而且还是一堂很有历史感的课。

segments.en: It's just a little bit of a culture and maybe some insight on American history.
segments.zh: 算是一点点文化，也许还有一些对美国历史的了解。

segments.en: It's not like we're politically active or anything, but yeah, it was some interesting information there.
segments.zh: 并不是说我们热衷政治或别的什么，不过，那里的确有些有趣的信息。

segments.en: And also, well, he was considered to be a pretty good president.
segments.zh: 而且，好吧，他被认为是一位相当优秀的总统。

segments.en: Yeah, he's rated, I wouldn't say among the top five or so, but quite accomplished.
segments.zh: 是的，他排不上前五名左右，但也相当有建树。

segments.en: Well, maybe not the greatest president we've ever seen, but he wrote a pretty good farewell speech.
segments.zh: 好吧，也许不是我们见过的最伟大的总统，但他写了一篇很好的告别演讲。

segments.en: So I think we have that to thank him for.
segments.zh: 所以我认为我们要感谢他。

segments.en: All right, guys, so if you have any other questions or comments, you can come to the website at EnglishPod.com and you can leave them there for Erica or I.
segments.zh: 好吧，伙计们，如果您有任何其他问题或意见，您可以访问 englishpod.com 的网站，您可以将它们留在那里给 Erica 或我。

segments.en: Okay, so thanks for downloading you guys and until next time, goodbye.
segments.zh: 好的，感谢大家的下载，下次再见，拜拜。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
